profile.reading:
This facility is mapped as CenturyLink, retaining the pre-Lumen brand name, at 2543 South Lamb Boulevard, Las Vegas, NV 89121, in Clark County; Lumen does not publish individual building addresses or specs on its own site for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites. CenturyLink was renamed Lumen Technologies on September 14, 2020, with its stock ticker changing from CTL to LUMN four days later; some legacy facility signage and mapping records, including this one, still carry the pre-rebrand CenturyLink name. Lumen's own colocation data sheet states more than 175 carrier-neutral data centers across more than 60 North American markets, offering cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range described as varying by site; unlike the wholesale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, Lumen does not disclose per-building square footage or total MW capacity for any of its sites.

Clark County, home to this Lumen/CenturyLink building, has its own active 2026 data center policy debate distinct from the Storey County tax-abatement submarket near Reno. Switch operates 11 data centers spanning more than 2 million square feet in the Las Vegas area; Clark County commissioners approved a roughly 57,000-square-foot expansion of an existing Switch facility in southwest Las Vegas on June 17, 2026 after public opposition, and on July 7, 2026 directed staff to study new land-use and environmental standards for data centers amid growing calls for regulation. Data centers accounted for about 22% of Nevada's electricity consumption in 2024, with NV Energy projecting statewide data center load could reach 64% of the utility's electricity sales by 2046, per Nevada Independent and FOX5 Las Vegas reporting.

Las Vegas' Clark County submarket sits jurisdictionally apart from the tax-abated Storey County campuses near Reno that dominate Nevada's hyperscale data center headlines, giving this older CenturyLink-branded building a more urban, network-edge role than the rural power-driven builds elsewhere in the state.

reading.body:
Lumen operates this Las Vegas facility under the legacy CenturyLink brand name at 2543 South Lamb Boulevard in Clark County. Lumen does not publish individual building power capacity, square footage, or IT load for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites, so this facility's relevance to AI scaling cannot be quantified from operator disclosures. The site offers cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range, which positions it as network-edge colocation rather than hyperscale compute infrastructure.

Clark County, where this facility sits, is a distinct regulatory jurisdiction from the tax-abated Storey County campuses near Reno that host Nevada's major wholesale data center builds. Switch operates 11 data centers spanning more than 2 million square feet in the Las Vegas area, and Clark County commissioners directed staff in July 2026 to study new land-use and environmental standards for data centers following public opposition to expansion. This older urban colocation site operates in a market increasingly focused on regulation rather than growth.

Data centers consumed about 22 percent of Nevada's electricity in 2024, with NV Energy projecting data center load could reach 64 percent of statewide utility sales by 2046. This facility's role in that trajectory is opaque because Lumen publishes no capacity data. Two of Nevada's 26 mapped data centers publish MW figures totaling 10.37 MW across the state, leaving 24 facilities including this one unmeasured and their contribution to Nevada's AI compute infrastructure unknown.
